en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Parimaṇḍalavagga 1.
The Training Rule on Being Evenly Rounded.
Now, venerable friends, these rules of training come up for recitation.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were wearing their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the recluses, sons of the Sakyans, wear their lower robes trailing both in front and behind, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?
The monks heard those people grumbling, complaining, and spreading it about.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and spread it about:
“How can the group-of-six monks wear their lower robes trailing both in front and behind?
Then those monks, having rebuked the group-of-six monks in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, on that occasion and for this reason, having convened the community of monks, questioned the group-of-six monks:
“Is it true, monks, that you wear your lower robes hanging down both in front and behind?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you wear your lower robes hanging down both in front and behind?
This, foolish men, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“The training is to be observed: ‘I shall put on the lower robe evenly all around.
It should be put on evenly all around, covering the navel and the knees.
Whoever, out of disrespect, puts it on hanging down in front or behind, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”
There is no offense if it was unintentional or due to lack of mindfulness.
For one who does not know,
for one who is ill,
and in times of distress.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The first training rule is concluded.
